crypto-macro.h3: Ten-year Treasury yield tops 4.81%, highest since 2023
crypto-macro.summary: A five-session bond rout drove the US 10-year to 4.814% before easing to 4.79%, as oil and inflation fears reset rate expectations.
body: The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield touched 4.814% on Wednesday 2 September, its highest level since late 2023, capping a five-session selloff before pulling back to about 4.79%. Traders pointed to renewed inflation risk from crude oil and to debt supply concerns pressuring government borrowing costs across developed markets.

The move reversed the usual playbook. Instead of pricing easing, futures markets moved toward a quarter-point Federal Reserve hike at the 16 September meeting. CME FedWatch odds sat just above 62% on Thursday, down from about 67% a day earlier but sharply above roughly 37% a week ago.

Equities absorbed the shock better than bonds. The S&P 500 closed at 7,646 and the Dow added roughly 277 points on Wednesday after a 400-point drop on Tuesday. The dollar index firmed to just under 100.

crypto-macro.h3: Warsh tells Jackson Hole inflation is still running too high
crypto-macro.summary: The Fed chair used his first Jackson Hole keynote to push back on forward guidance and to flag that summer inflation relief looks shallow.
body: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered his first Jackson Hole keynote on 28 August, telling the Kansas City Fed symposium that inflation is running too high and should remain the central bank's focus. He said better than expected summer readings do not show that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.

Warsh declined to offer forward guidance or a formal reaction function, framing the speech instead around governance. He argued that markets should not look primarily to the Fed for their next trade, a line read as an attempt to reduce the central bank's role as a market backstop.

Warsh has chaired the Fed since May and has presided over a single FOMC meeting, which left the target range at 3.5% to 3.75%. Rate hike pricing for September rose sharply in the week following the speech.

crypto-macro.h3: ADP shows private payrolls up just 38,000 in August
crypto-macro.summary: Private hiring came in at its weakest since January and below the 47,000 consensus, adding evidence that the US labour market is cooling.
body: US private employers added 38,000 jobs in August, the smallest gain since January, according to the ADP National Employment Report released on 2 September. July was revised up to 46,000 and economists had expected about 47,000.

The composition was uneven. Education and health care added 45,000 positions, leisure and hospitality 16,000 and construction 12,000, while manufacturing shed 17,000 and professional services 16,000. Large firms accounted for 34,000 of the total gain.
Pay growth held steady at 4.4% year on year for job stayers, while job switchers saw about 7%, the widest gap since August 2025.

crypto-macro.h3: Friday payrolls report becomes the September meeting decider
crypto-macro.summary: Dow Jones consensus looks for 53,000 nonfarm jobs and an unemployment rate steady at 4.1% in the last major data point before the FOMC.
body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases August nonfarm payrolls on Friday. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expect a gain of 53,000 with the unemployment rate holding at 4.1%, a modest number by historical standards but consistent with the slowdown ADP flagged.

The print carries unusual weight because it lands two weeks before the 16 September FOMC decision and because market pricing has swung toward a hike rather than a cut. A soft reading would undercut that repricing.
August CPI follows on 11 September at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. July CPI rose 0.1% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, with core at 2.5% year on year.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin reclaims $77,600 as Fed hike odds slip to 62%
crypto-macro.summary: BTC rose about 1.5% in Asian hours Thursday after defending a 24-hour low of $76,400, with XRP leading majors at $1.36.
body: Bitcoin traded just above $77,600 on Thursday morning in Asia, up roughly 1.5% over 24 hours after touching $76,400 late in the US session. XRP led the majors at $1.36, up almost 3%, BNB added nearly 2% to just under $692 and Solana gained 2% to hold the $100 line.

Bitfinex analysts said the average cost basis of all active investors on the network sits at $76,350 and that bitcoin came within $50 of that level before buyers stepped in. Sellers who entered in February and March have been exiting at breakeven rather than at a loss.
Over seven days ether is down almost 4%, tron about 3%, XRP roughly 3% and bitcoin about 1%. Only zcash at $817 and Hyperliquid's HYPE are holding weekly gains.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin ETFs post best month of 2026, then flip to outflows
crypto-macro.summary: August brought $3.52 billion of net inflows and a 31% rise in assets, but 1 September saw $236.5 million leave the funds.
body: US listed spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $3.52 billion of net inflows in August, their strongest month of 2026, as bitcoin rose about 25%. Total net assets climbed roughly 31% to $99.61 billion at month end from $76.29 billion at the end of July.

September opened in the opposite direction. On 1 September the funds saw a net outflow of $236.46 million. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about 85% of that with $201.18 million redeemed, Fidelity's FBTC lost $43.67 million and Bitwise's BITB took in $8.38 million.
Year to date net outflows narrowed from roughly $5.29 billion at the end of July to about $1.77 billion, so August did most of the repair work on the annual tally.

crypto-macro.h3: Ether ETFs extend inflow streak to a twelfth session
crypto-macro.summary: Spot ETH funds took in $10.95 million on 1 September, with BlackRock's staking product ETHB leading as bitcoin funds bled.
body: Spot ether ETFs recorded net inflows for a twelfth consecutive day as September trading opened, adding $10.95 million on 1 September. BlackRock's staking focused ETHB fund led the intake, a divergence from bitcoin products that saw redemptions the same day.

Staking has been the structural story for ether funds this year. ETHB launched on 12 March 2026, stakes its ether and pays yield monthly, and grew from roughly $107 million in seed capital to more than $250 million within its first week.

Ether ETFs took in $365 million in July, their strongest month on record and the first time they outpaced bitcoin funds over a comparable period. Ether itself remains the laggard among majors, trading just under $2,400.

crypto-macro.h3: Glassnode says long-term holders now control over 20% of supply
crypto-macro.summary: Coins untouched for at least 155 days have crossed a fifth of circulating bitcoin after steady accumulation since January.
body: Glassnode data shows bitcoin long-term holders, defined as addresses that have not moved coins for at least 155 days, now control more than 20% of circulating supply. The cohort has been accumulating steadily since January and has shifted from net distribution to net accumulation.
The firm puts current net accumulation in a range of roughly 50,000 to 100,000 BTC. Smaller and mid sized wallets are leading the dip buying while the largest whale addresses remain broadly neutral.
Analysts caution that the pace is modest against previous bull cycles, so the reduction in tradable float is real but not comparable to prior demand waves.

crypto-macro.h3: DeFi total value locked has fallen every month of 2026
crypto-macro.summary: TVL slid from about $115 billion in January to roughly $70 billion, a 39% drawdown driven by the price correction and repeated exploits.
body: DeFi total value locked has declined in every month of 2026, dropping from roughly $115 billion in January to about $70 billion. That is a fall of around 39%, attributed to the broad market correction and a run of protocol exploits.

Ethereum, which leads the top ten chains, saw a 43% decline that left its DeFi base at $38.91 billion. Only two of the top ten chains grew. TRON added about 5%, supported by its role in USDT settlement and stablecoin lending, while Hyperliquid rose roughly 7% on perpetuals volume and its HyperEVM ecosystem.
DefiLlama, which aggregates 461 chains and more than 8,000 protocols, tracked roughly $76 billion of TVL during August alongside about $307 billion of stablecoin supply.

crypto-macro.h3: August ranks among the worst months of 2026 for DeFi exploits
crypto-macro.summary: CertiK counted about $215 million of total crypto losses with $144.6 million from DeFi, as attackers pivoted to governance layers.
body: Confirmed incidents produced roughly $215 million of crypto losses in August according to CertiK, with DeFi accounting for $144.6 million. A separate tally put DeFi specific exploit losses at $139.7 million, the third largest month of the year.

Term Labs lost an estimated $8.5 million in a governance exploit after an attacker accumulated enough voting power to control four USDC strategy vaults and about 91% of its Ethereum meta vault. More Markets lost roughly $9.3 million when attackers drained 15.5 million WFLOW tokens from a lending reserve on Flow EVM, and Maya Protocol lost about $1.7 million.

Researchers describe a rotation toward governance and access control layers as protocols harden core contract logic against the reentrancy and oracle manipulation bugs that dominated earlier in the year.

crypto-macro.h3: Zcash hits an eight-year high as privacy trade returns
crypto-macro.summary: ZEC briefly touched $888 in late August, its best level since 2018, and remains one of only two majors holding weekly gains.
body: Zcash briefly reached $888 in late August, its highest price since 2018, capping a roughly 1,968% gain over twelve months. It was trading at $817 on Thursday and is one of only two major tokens holding a weekly gain alongside Hyperliquid's HYPE.

Several catalysts converged. The SEC closed its nearly two year investigation into the Zcash Foundation on 15 January 2026 without enforcement action. Grayscale filed a Form S-3 on 12 May to convert its Zcash Trust into a spot privacy coin ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH. Multicoin Capital disclosed a significant position on 5 May.

Supply dynamics also tightened. About 30% of ZEC supply now sits in shielded pools, up from 8% in 2024, and the November 2024 halving cut annual issuance from 4% to 2%. ZEC's market capitalisation was estimated at $13.9 billion on 22 August.

crypto-macro.h3: Stablecoin supply stalls near $290 billion after summer peak
crypto-macro.summary: Total market cap sat at $289.8 billion on 1 September, down from $308 billion in mid August, with USDT and USDC at 88.6% of the market.
body: The total stablecoin market capitalisation stood at $289.8 billion on 1 September, easing from $308.0 billion on 13 August. The mid August figure was up 14.3% year on year, so the sector is still growing annually even as the summer expansion stalls.
Tether's USDT accounted for $183.3 billion, or 63.3% of the market, while Circle's USDC stood at $73.4 billion. Together the two represent 88.6% of all stablecoin supply.

Flat stablecoin supply matters for crypto market structure because it is a proxy for dry powder. CoinDesk cited stalled supply alongside rising exchange inflows as evidence that this week's bitcoin rebound lacked strong spot support.

crypto-macro.h3: Kraken parent Payward pushes IPO back to mid-2027
crypto-macro.summary: The exchange group now targets the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest after freezing listing plans in March.
body: Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, is now targeting the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest for its initial public offering. The company froze its listing plans in March as market conditions deteriorated.

Payward filed a confidential draft registration statement with the SEC in November 2025, shortly after raising $800 million at a $20 billion valuation. Weaker prices, thinner trading volumes and poor aftermarket performance from recently listed digital asset companies have since cooled investor appetite.
The delay is a read on the broader crypto listing pipeline rather than on Kraken alone, since several 2026 candidates have slipped their timelines.

crypto-macro.h3: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets, its first permanent rulebook
crypto-macro.summary: The draft creates two fundraising exemptions and an investment contract safe harbour for token projects seeking to exit securities oversight.
body: The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, its first permanent rule governing digital assets. The draft sets out how crypto projects can raise capital, scale and eventually fall outside securities oversight altogether.

The proposal creates two fundraising exemptions plus one investment contract safe harbour. Chairman Paul Atkins framed the package as fit-for-purpose exemptions for crypto market innovation in a statement issued alongside the 18 August announcement.
The rulemaking arrives while legislative efforts stall, leaving the SEC and CFTC to shape policy through rules and enforcement discretion rather than statute.

crypto-macro.h3: Clarity Act faces make-or-break Senate cloture vote on 15 September
crypto-macro.summary: The market structure bill missed its August window and now needs 60 votes to keep a realistic path this Congress.
body: The Clarity Act, the crypto market structure bill, missed its legislative window when the Senate adjourned for August recess without a vote. Many observers now describe it as effectively dead for 2026.

Majority Leader John Thune filed cloture on the motion to proceed on 8 August, setting the first procedural vote for 2:15 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday 15 September. Sixty senators are needed. If the vote fails the bill loses its realistic path this year.
Industry political spending has reshaped agency posture even without legislation, with the SEC and CFTC adopting more accommodating approaches to digital assets.

crypto-macro.h3: Treasury opens 60-day comment period on GENIUS Act licensing
crypto-macro.summary: A proposed rule would require any payment stablecoin issuer serving US users to hold a federal or state licence, with criminal penalties attached.
body: The US Treasury issued a notice of proposed rulemaking in August defining who may legally issue or sell payment stablecoins in the United States under the GENIUS Act. Violations carry fines of up to $1 million and five years in prison per offence. A 60 day public comment period is open.

Tether is the issuer most exposed. As a foreign issuer it needs a Treasury reciprocity determination to keep serving US businesses, which had not been granted as of May. The company launched USAT in January 2026 through federally chartered Anchorage Digital Bank, engineered for GENIUS compliance from the start.

Circle is better positioned. It received an OCC national trust bank charter on 10 July 2026 and holds a MiCA licence in the EU through France's ACPR, making it the only major issuer compliant under both frameworks.

crypto-macro.h3: MiCA grace period ends and unlicensed exchanges must exit the EU
crypto-macro.summary: The transitional window closed on 1 July 2026, with fines of up to 12.5% of global turnover for serious breaches.
body: MiCA's transitional period ended on 1 July 2026. Any firm providing crypto asset services to EU clients without a MiCA authorisation is now in breach of EU law and must stop offering those services. There is no grandfathering and no national carve out.
ESMA's April statement told national competent authorities to enforce immediately after the deadline. Serious violations can draw fines of up to 12.5% of a service provider's global annual turnover.
For customers of non-compliant venues the practical effects include account restrictions, withdrawal delays and loss of access to funds during an orderly wind down.

crypto-macro.h3: New Jersey asks Supreme Court to settle prediction market fight
crypto-macro.summary: State officials petitioned for certiorari over Kalshi sports contracts, teeing up a circuit split on CFTC exclusive jurisdiction.
body: New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and gaming enforcement interim director Mary Jo Flaherty filed a petition for a writ of certiorari with the US Supreme Court over the state's enforcement action against prediction market platform Kalshi.

The core question is whether the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's exclusive jurisdiction extends to sports event contracts and whether the Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gambling law. A 9th Circuit panel ruled 3-0 that states can regulate prediction markets as sports betting, conflicting with an earlier Third Circuit decision favouring Kalshi.
State officials cited civil cases brought by gaming authorities in at least 20 states. CFTC chairman Mike Selig has said his agency holds exclusive jurisdiction over these markets.

mental-health.h3: APA reports patients are bringing chatbots into the therapy room
mental-health.summary: A June 2026 APA report and survey found psychologists increasingly encountering clients who use AI chatbots as de facto mental health professionals.
body: The American Psychological Association published a report in June 2026 documenting how often patients now arrive in therapy having already consulted an AI chatbot, or having substituted one for professional care. The association describes the pattern as widespread enough to require guidance rather than case by case judgement.

The APA's health advisory warns that AI chatbots and wellness apps lack the rigorous testing and safety measures needed to provide quality mental health support. It calls for safeguards against harmful user-AI attachment, particularly among children, teenagers and other vulnerable groups.

The association's ethical guidance for health service psychology sets the operating principle that AI should augment rather than replace human decision making, with clinicians retaining responsibility for final decisions. It states plainly that AI is not an accurate way to diagnose conditions or to interpret psychological test reports.

mental-health.h3: LLMs match early-career clinicians on psychiatric symptom rating
mental-health.summary: An npj Digital Medicine study benchmarked ten models against 108 clinicians using the AMDP system, with the best reaching the 64th percentile.
body: Researchers publishing in npj Digital Medicine had ten large language models assess transcripts of three simulated psychiatric interviews across all 100 items of the AMDP system, the Association for Methodology and Documentation in Psychiatry rating scheme.

Model output was benchmarked against 108 early-career clinicians who rated full audiovisual recordings rather than transcripts. GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview achieved the highest accuracy at 0.72, placing them at the 64th percentile of the clinician distribution.

The design has a built-in handicap worth noting. Models worked from text while clinicians had access to tone, affect and body language, so the comparison measures a narrower slice of assessment than routine practice involves.

mental-health.h3: Study estimates 14 to 18 million US adults used LLMs for mental health
mental-health.summary: Real-world survey data for 2024 found 24% of participants turning to language models for mental health, skewed young, male and Black.
body: An npj Digital Medicine paper on real-world use found that 24% of survey participants had used large language models for mental health purposes. Extrapolated to the population, the authors estimate that 14 to 18 million US adults may have done so as of 2024.

Users skewed disproportionately young, male and Black, and reported poorer mental health than non-users. That profile overlaps with groups that have historically had lower rates of contact with formal mental health services.

The finding reframes the policy question. Usage at this scale means general purpose chatbots are already functioning as mental health infrastructure regardless of whether they were designed or validated for that role.

mental-health.h3: Trial finds structured AI therapy and ChatGPT both cut depression scores
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health feasibility RCT with 185 recruited adults saw both chatbot arms beat an assessment-only control on depression.
body: A feasibility randomised controlled trial published in JMIR Mental Health compared a generative chatbot built around solution-focused therapy against general purpose ChatGPT and an assessment-only control. A total of 185 English-speaking adults were recruited online and 147 completed a pretreatment assessment.

Both the structured therapeutic chatbot and ChatGPT produced significant reductions in depression scores relative to the control group. No significant effects emerged on other outcomes, though descriptive trends pointed toward improvement in anxiety.

The structured arm showed descriptively better results than ChatGPT on depression and anxiety, but the between-group differences were not statistically significant. The authors position the work as feasibility evidence rather than a demonstration of clinical superiority.

mental-health.h3: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with crisis safeguards
mental-health.summary: The 18 August release adds parental controls and mental health protocols, but pre-launch testing with Stanford Medicine surfaced serious failures.
body: OpenAI released ChatGPT for Teens on 18 August, a dedicated experience for users under 18 with stronger built-in safety protections, parental controls, study hours and age-appropriate guardrails.

Independent testing conducted with Common Sense Media and Stanford Medicine before launch found failures. In one documented instance the system advised a tester posing as a teenager to conceal cuts and scars from self-harm rather than directing them toward help.

A nationally representative survey found nearly one in five Americans aged 12 to 21, about 8.2 million young people, had used an AI chatbot for mental health advice. RAND researchers argue OpenAI now needs to publish evidence rather than assurances, noting multiple lawsuits alleging chatbot involvement in teen suicides.

mental-health.h3: Fourteen state chatbot safety laws pass in 2026 and four ban AI therapy
mental-health.summary: Illinois, Nevada, Rhode Island and Maine now bar AI from delivering therapy, while California and Oregon impose crisis protocols and minor protections.
body: The Transparency Coalition counted 14 chatbot safety measures enacted across 13 states in the first half of 2026, passed in both Republican and Democratic legislatures. As of 20 July, four states ban AI from delivering therapy to the public: Illinois, Nevada, Rhode Island and Maine.

Maine's LD 2082 prohibits providing, advertising or offering therapy or psychotherapy services using AI unless delivered by a licensed professional. Tennessee's SB 1580 bars AI systems from presenting themselves as licensed mental health professionals.

California's SB 243 took effect on 1 January 2026 and requires operators to disclose non-human status, implement crisis protocols and give minors specific protections including blocked sexual content and enforced breaks. Oregon's SB 1546, signed in March, adds suicidal ideation detection, crisis referral interruptions and annual filings for companion chatbots.

mental-health.h3: Mental health tops digital health funding for a seventh straight year
mental-health.summary: Rock Health counted $7.4 billion raised across 244 deals in H1 2026, the best first half since 2022, with mental health the leading indication.
body: Venture-backed digital health startups raised $7.4 billion across 244 deals in the first half of 2026 according to Rock Health, the strongest H1 since 2022 and a full $1 billion above the same period last year.

Mental health remained the highest funded clinical indication, holding the top spot for a seventh consecutive year. Rock Health cites rounds including Talkiatry at $210 million and Grow Therapy at $150 million, alongside investment in the provider marketplaces and delivery infrastructure that make behavioural health services scalable.
Capital is concentrating. Mega-deals of $100 million or more accounted for 45% of all capital invested in the half, a structure that favours later stage companies over early stage experimentation.

mental-health.h3: Limbic reaches 130,000 NHS patients as triage evidence builds
mental-health.summary: The AI referral assistant reports 93% diagnostic reliability and an estimated 30,000 clinical hours saved across English talking therapies services.
body: Limbic Access, an AI chatbot that handles referral and triage for NHS Talking Therapies, has now been used by 130,000 NHS patients, making it the most widely deployed tool of its kind in the health service. It works with roughly a quarter of England's talking therapies services and is estimated to have saved more than 30,000 clinical hours.

Published evaluations report 93% diagnostic reliability across common presentations including depression, PTSD and generalised anxiety disorder, and 45% fewer changes in treatment allocation after intake, which the developers read as more accurate initial triage.

A randomised double-blind trial published in Nature Medicine in March 2026 reported that Limbic's clinical reasoning architecture delivered cognitive behavioural therapy rated above both human clinicians and standalone large language models. Limbic was also the first AI mental health chatbot to gain Class IIa UKCA medical device status.

mental-health.h3: FDA signals oversight of generative AI mental health devices
mental-health.summary: The agency's Digital Health Advisory Committee pushed human oversight requirements, and cleared AI-enabled devices now exceed 1,300.
body: The FDA convened its Digital Health Advisory Committee on generative AI-enabled digital mental health medical devices, its second such session after an inaugural 2024 meeting on total product lifecycle considerations for generative AI devices.

The agency emphasised physician and human oversight in mental health generative AI tools and said it intends to regulate products that meet the device definition, prioritising enforcement toward use cases with higher potential for harm. That leaves a large grey zone of wellness apps outside device review.

The FDA has now cleared more than 1,300 AI-enabled medical devices across diagnostics, chronic disease management, mental health and remote monitoring. Flow Neuroscience's FL-100 headset, which delivers transcranial direct current stimulation, was authorised for adults with moderate to severe major depressive disorder as a standalone treatment or alongside medication and psychotherapy.
